description: types.rs:60-219 — QuotaScope (RFC 9425), ChatMemberRole (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00), and BodyType (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00) each carry the same ~50-line block: enum decl + as_str() + Display + Serialize + Deserialize, all matching the same pattern (typed variants + Other/Unknown(String) catch-all, hex-string-equivalent serde behaviour). All three are JMAP-native wire enums, so they correctly use the typed-enum-with-catch-all pattern (workspace policy excludes only RFC 9553/8984 externally-owned classifier strings, not these). The pattern duplication is ~150 lines that an internal macro would collapse to ~30. The Rust review guide explicitly approves of internal macros that replace repetition. A 'wire_enum! { QuotaScope { Account => "account", Domain => "domain", Global => "global", Other(_) }, ChatMemberRole { ... }, BodyType { ... } }' macro would generate all four impls. Engineering basis: every future wire enum added to this crate (or sibling crates) is currently a copy-paste with a different variant set — the macro removes that copy-paste burden and centralises the catch-all-naming policy. Workspace consideration: if sibling crates use the same pattern, the macro belongs in jmap-types as a re-exported macro_rules!.
title: Three near-identical wire-enum impl blocks for QuotaScope/ChatMemberRole/BodyType
